PASS-WITH-NOTES -- performance, round 2 (final under C34), PR #306
Head: 89a82bf8ec10ca7ba8902f2070df7efb8560542f
Reviewed change: 8af888e2^..8af888e2, excluding the unrelated main merges.

The round-one cost-wording note is CLOSED. The revised cost row matches the code. No new performance finding or blocker.

Catalog-call proof

The canary's pane observation now passes None for native_session_id (crates/daemon/src/http/governance.rs:2158-2171). The adapter's catalog gate requires native_session_id.is_some() (crates/harnesses/src/adapter.rs:106-113), so this observation cannot invoke omp.models.

runtime_model (governance.rs:2002-2035) has mutually exclusive branches:

| Harness / footer / native | Catalog operation per model decision |
| --- | --- |
| OMP, nonempty parsed footer, eligible native | one shows(native, footer) |
| OMP, nonempty parsed footer, no eligible native | one resolve(footer) |
| OMP, no parsed model (or empty model) | zero |
| Any non-OMP harness | zero |

The native branch returns after shows, including an error from shows; it cannot then enter resolve. There is no catalog retry/fallback loop in the decision. Both concrete catalog methods use the shared blocking wrapper (governance.rs:1960-1982), so the existing synchronous child wait and inventory parsing run on spawn_blocking, not the async reactor.

Both helpers reach the existing run_omp_command through one omp_inventory_with call (crates/harnesses/src/models.rs:445-497). That launch site remains unchanged: spawns::record("omp.models"), program::launch("omp", ...), and fixed arguments models --json --no-extensions, with the inherited five-second child timeout and ten-millisecond child-wait polling. It is at most one counted catalog invocation per qualifying canary, not one per seat, and not two when native and footer are both present. The inherited executable-resolution and counter-attempt limits from round one remain; no new launcher is added.

The revised row correctly retains the catalog charge on the native path: it is now an agreement check rather than footer-name resolution. With qualifying acknowledged OMP canary rate r/s, the added catalog rate against today's broken parser is at most r/s; with no such canaries, zero additional launches/s regardless of live-seat count. A refusal before this decision can cost less. "Zero" in the table means zero catalog launches, not zero unrelated existing delivery/process/tmux work in the whole canary.

Scheduling and native-read cost

No new loop, poll, timer, hook or per-tick/per-live-seat process launch. The production call graph still enters this decision only from canary_command. The new unknown-pending-switch check scans the SDK's existing fixed fact-name inventory on each existing seat-status projection; it introduces no IO, process or scheduler.

The native-read qualifications in the round-one receipt 40f84bb133ee0b9622d065be0712b49072eb7290 still apply: shared per-seat cursor, serialized incremental reads, no launch, cold/reset reads proportional to the transcript, no total-byte or end-to-end canary status-read deadline. Round two neither adds another status read nor changes the SDK dependency. No new constant-time or fixed-memory claim is made.

Verification

- just pr-freeze 306: FINAL at the full head above, clean detached worktree, all five latest CI checks passed.
- CI run 44854728831, attempt 1, successful rust-test job 136694135459; the run API confirms head 89a82bf8ec10ca7ba8902f2070df7efb8560542f.
- Downloaded junit-linux artifact 14687465695, selected from that successful job's upload log, not by artifact name. Ten selected cases passed: native_evidence_needs_no_footer_resolution; the_footer_answers_only_without_native_evidence; a_role_switch_the_record_does_not_see_refuses_until_the_next_call; omp_footer_checks_against_one_selector_without_resolving_the_name; an_undecided_switch_reads_as_pending; both spawn-site sensors; both warm/cancelled cursor regressions; and the HTTP governance canary integration case. These confirm test execution, not deployed latency or measured launch rates.
- CI cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci: passed. The source branch audit above establishes the at-most-one call bound; no new exhaustive/mutation gate was added in this final round.
- git diff --check: passed. No source changes, dependency installs/links, local builds, canaries, bounce, closures or kills. harness boot again reported ready:false because this C25 review worktree has no vitest. Local full harness/TS gates were not run and are not represented as passing.

Live-proof boundary and remaining note

This PR is still not deployed. A read-only live ping during this round confirmed the same baseline daemon PID 28181 at eb1ab2c60a, with no POST /v1/canary or omp.models counter entry. That is not execution proof for this head. The measured BEFORE window remains the round-one receipt: 2026-11-21T01:35:27.999420Z to 01:35:48.217135Z, 20.2129798339447 s; daemon spawns 770 -> 770 (every op flat), CPU +3.81 s (18.849% of one core), RSS 189600 -> 190432 KiB; the separate machine-probe report was 269.6 launches/s. It is not a round-two AFTER measurement.

Only the existing deployment measurement debt remains: the authorized deploy owner must repeat the counters, CPU/RSS and machine probe after deployment; an active-path canary must target an owned throwaway seat. No new performance work is required before merge. This is a performance-only verdict and does not decide the reviewer/security question about stale native evidence during a catalog outage.

Harness feedback: the useful enduring distinction is "no footer-name resolution" versus "no catalog invocation". A future read-only cost-receipt probe should report operation counts separately from the chosen native/footer evidence source. No harness/product mutation was made in this detached review tree.
